name: Abul Kalam Azad (Bachchu Razakar)
role: Fugitive ICT convict known as Bachchu Razakar
contribution: Abul Kalam Azad, known as Bachchu Razakar, was sentenced to death in absentia in the first ICT verdict for crimes against humanity and genocide charges connected to 1971.
context: Razakar collaboration allegations, the first International Crimes Tribunal verdict, and post-2010 war-crimes accountability politics in Bangladesh.
impact: His case became the opening judgment in Bangladesh's ICT process and is important to distinguish from the Indian nationalist scholar also named Abul Kalam Azad.
highlight: The first ICT verdict figure, distinct from Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

faq.question: Why does this profile use a distinct slug from Abul Kalam Azad?
faq.answer: The slug separates Bachchu Razakar, the fugitive ICT convict in a 1971 case, from Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the Indian nationalist scholar-politician already represented elsewhere in the figure set.
